3 Host tree The host phylogeny places species represented in the first and second EHI data releases within the wider set of vertebrate hosts recorded by the EHI. Hosts in the second release are shown at full opacity, species found only in the first release are translucent, and all remaining EHI hosts are retained as faint, unlabelled tips. 3.1 Host metadata Write the host species and taxonomic metadata linked to the current release. host_metadata %>% pull(host_species) %>% unique() %>% sort() %>% write_lines(file = str_c("data/", release, "_allhosts.txt")) host_metadata %>% write_tsv(file = str_c("data/", release, "_allhosts.tsv")) Combine the current host metadata with the host table archived from the first data release. Lepidosauria in the first-release table is standardised to Reptilia so that the two releases share the same class labels. ehr01_host_metadata <- read_tsv( "data/EHR01_host.tsv", show_col_types=FALSE ) ehi_host_species <- read_lines("data/EHI_allhosts.txt") %>% str_squish() tree_name_substitutions <- c( "Bombina sp."="Bombina_variegata", "Canis familiaris"="Canis_lupus", "Psammodromus manuelae"="Psammodromus_hispanicus", "Salamandra salamandra gallaica"="Salamandra_salamandra" ) host_tree_metadata <- bind_rows( host_metadata %>% mutate(metadata_priority=1L), ehr01_host_metadata %>% mutate(metadata_priority=2L) ) %>% arrange(metadata_priority) %>% distinct(host_species, .keep_all=TRUE) %>% select(-metadata_priority) %>% mutate( host_class=recode(host_class, "Lepidosauria"="Reptilia"), tree_tip=if_else( host_species %in% names(tree_name_substitutions), unname(tree_name_substitutions[host_species]), str_replace_all(host_species, " ", "_") ), release_status=if_else( host_species %in% host_metadata$host_species, "Second data release", "First data release only" ), display_label=host_species ) Four names absent from the TimeTree backbone use explicit taxonomic substitutions: Bombina sp. is placed as B. variegata, Canis familiaris as C. lupus, Psammodromus manuelae as P. hispanicus, and Salamandra salamandra gallaica as S. salamandra. 3.2 Combined time-calibrated phylogeny The phylogenetic backbone is the time-calibrated tetrapod tree from TimeTree (Kumar et al. 2022), pruned to all resolvable EHI vertebrate hosts. This retains the broad EHI context used in the first data release while adding all hosts represented in EHR02. host_tree_path <- "data/EHI_EHR01_EHR02_allhosts.nwk" if (!file.exists(host_tree_path)) { stop("Combined EHI host tree not found: ", host_tree_path) } all_host_tree <- read_tree(host_tree_path) unmatched_tree_hosts <- host_tree_metadata %>% filter(!tree_tip %in% all_host_tree$tip.label) if (nrow(unmatched_tree_hosts) > 0) { stop( "Hosts missing from the combined tree: ", paste(unmatched_tree_hosts$host_species, collapse=", ") ) } The archived EHI host catalogue contains 375 names, of which 293 resolve as distinct tips in the phylogenetic backbone.
